public-safety-administration-certificate.tileDesc: Build management skills for public safety
public-safety-administration-certificate.name: Public Safety Administration
public-safety-administration-certificate.lead: Build leadership and management skills for emergency services and public safety organizations.
public-safety-administration-certificate.learn: Learn how to lead teams, manage emergencies, streamline operations and support fire and emergency operations. During your studies, you will gain skills in: Incident management; Command; leadership; budgeting.

rows.name: Law Enforcement Management & Supervision
rows.desc: This course provides a study of the best known methods and practices of police leadership and management. Topics include the role of the manager in law enforcement, communications, time-management in law enforcement, managing problems, training and law enforcement productivity. Upon completion, students should be able to identify and discuss methods and practices capable of moving law enforcement agencies forward into the twenty-first century.

rows.name: Emergency Management
rows.desc: This course covers the four phases of emergency management: mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. Topics include organizing for emergency management, coordinating for community resources, public sector liability, and the roles of government agencies at all levels. Upon completion, students should be able to demonstrate an understanding of comprehensive emergency management and the integrated emergency management system.

rows.name: Introduction to Public Administration
rows.desc: This course includes an overview of the role of the public administrator in government and an examination of the development and implementation of public policy. Topics include public personnel administration and management, decision making, public affairs, ethics, organizational theories, budgetary functions within governmental agencies, and other governmental issues. Upon completion, students should be able to explain the functions of government in society and in the lives of people composing that society.

rows.name: Ethics in Government
rows.desc: This course introduces the ethical issues and problems within the public administration field. Emphasis is placed on building analytical skills, stimulating moral imagination, and recognizing the discretionary power of the administrator's role. Upon completion, students should be able to understand the moral dimensions of public administrative decision making.

rows.name: Public Finance & Budgeting
rows.desc: This course provides an overview of the public finance and budgeting processes used in the allocation of public resources to meet differing public interests. Topics include the political environment, government expenditures, revenues, taxation, budgetary process theories and techniques, and the relation of government finance to the economy. Upon completion, students should be able to recognize impacts of government revenue and expenditure policies and understand the role of budgeting in executing governmental policy.

Topics include federal, state, and local roles and responsibilities in major disaster, response, and recovery work, with an emphasis on governmental coordination. Upon completion, students should be able to implement a disaster response plan and assess the needs of those involved in a major disaster.

ce.label: Career Training & Certifications
ce.tagline: Non-credit training for new and working first responders in law enforcement, fire, rescue, and EMS.

courses.name: Basic Law Enforcement Training
courses.desc: Start a law enforcement career with hands-on training in criminal law, investigations, patrol procedures, emergency response, and ethics. The program meets weekdays for about 16 weeks and prepares you for North Carolina law enforcement certification.

courses.name: Police Assistance Company Training
courses.desc: Learn how first responders and community members support local, regional, and federal law enforcement officers. The class reviews recent events through after action reports and covers unified command.

courses.name: Public Safety Bike Patrol (LEBA)
courses.desc: Complete the basic training for Class C bike patrol certification. Fire personnel and security officers finish a written and practical exam after two days of bike training.

courses.name: Emergency Medical Responder
courses.desc: Take the first step into EMS with the initial Emergency Medical Responder course. The course follows the standards of the North Carolina Office of Emergency Medical Services.

courses.name: Emergency Medical Technician
courses.desc: Train to the level of Emergency Medical Technician. Learn the skills to provide basic life support with an ambulance service or other specialized service.

courses.name: Advanced Emergency Medical Technician
courses.desc: Provide basic and limited advanced emergency care and transport for critical patients. Advanced EMTs work as part of a full EMS response under medical oversight.

courses.name: EMT Refresher
courses.desc: Review the core modules of the initial EMT course. Topics include airway, patient assessment, medical and behavioral care, trauma, and obstetrics, infants, and children.

courses.name: Paramedic Refresher
courses.desc: Review the knowledge and skills required at the paramedic level. This hybrid course pairs 16 classroom hours with 104 online hours and follows North Carolina Office of EMS standards.

courses.name: Critical Care Transport
courses.desc: Prepare paramedics and nurses to serve on a critical care transport team. Learn to keep critical patients and hospital equipment stable between facilities.

courses.name: Flight Paramedic Exam Prep
courses.desc: Prepare for the Flight Paramedic Certification (FP-C) exam in a 36-hour online course. The course also serves as a refresher for current critical care paramedics.

courses.name: Basic Life Support (CPR)
courses.desc: Earn the American Red Cross Basic Life Support credential. Learn to recognize and care for cardiac arrest, respiratory emergencies, airway obstruction, and opioid overdose.

courses.name: Hazardous Materials Technician
courses.desc: Take offensive action at hazardous materials incidents. Training covers chemical identification, protective gear, leak control, and decontamination.

courses.name: Rope Rescue Technician
courses.desc: Train in advanced high-angle and vertical rope rescue. The course follows NFPA 1006 and the North Carolina Office of State Fire Marshal guidelines.

courses.name: Firefighter Functional Challenge
courses.desc: Test yourself against the physical demands of structural firefighting. Students wear full bunker gear and breathing apparatus through timed obstacle courses.

courses.name: Emergency Vehicle Driver Training
courses.desc: Learn to operate SUVs and quick response vehicles safely during emergency response. Build the driving skills that protect crews, equipment, and the public.

courses.name: Animal Rescue
courses.desc: Learn the skills specialized responders use to save animals during disasters and crises. Topics include animal rescue, shelter operations, and reuniting animals with owners.

courses.name: NIMS: ICS-100
courses.desc: Learn the history, principles, and structure of the Incident Command System. This course is the foundation for all higher-level ICS training.

courses.name: NIMS: ICS-200
courses.desc: Prepare to take a supervisory role in the Incident Command System during initial response. The course builds on ICS-100.

courses.name: Emergency Response Skills and Evaluation
courses.desc: Practice and evaluate emergency response through discussion-based and hands-on exercises. Measure performance against clear objectives and improve emergency plans.

courses.name: Intelligently Aggressive Incident Command
courses.desc: Prepare fire officers to command large incidents with limited staff and budgets. The course addresses the growing demands on fire departments.
